title: Merge Maintenance Slots
statement: Several teams booked maintenance windows on the same server. Each booking is a closed interval `[l, r]` of integer minutes, which includes both endpoints.

Combine bookings that overlap into a single window. Two bookings overlap when they share at least one minute, so `[1, 3]` and `[3, 5]` merge into `[1, 5]`. Bookings that only touch as neighbours, such as `[1, 2]` and `[3, 4]`, stay separate.
Print the merged windows sorted by their left endpoint.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `l r`.
outputFormat: On the first line print `k`, the number of merged windows.
Then print `k` lines, each with `l r` for one merged window, sorted by `l`.
constraints: Bookings are given in any order. The output can contain up to 100001 lines, so build it efficiently (for example with a string builder) instead of printing one value at a time with flushing.

examples.explanation: [2,2] lies inside [1,2]; [3,4] only touches it and stays separate.

input: Next n lines: l r (closed interval)
starter.output: k, then k lines 'l r' sorted by l

private.complexity: O(n log n) sort by left endpoint, then one merge pass. Repeatedly merging pairs is O(n^2) and times out.
private.notes: Merge when next.l <= current.r (closed intervals). Extend current.r with max, because a nested interval can end earlier.
